$SMH Trade Ideas: Nov 27 550C and Nov 6 500P

BULLISH: Nov 27 550C
Trigger: hold or reclaim 525 ✅
Targets: 538, 550 🎯
Stop: 515 🛑

BEARISH: Nov 6 500P
Trigger: lose 525 and reject the retest ✅
Targets: 515, 500 🎯
Stop: 527 🛑

Buyers had their chance to push higher this week. They couldn't hold it.

Now we're back at a key decision point.

Last week, I highlighted 538, 525, and 500.

SMH closed this week at $527.20, just above that second level. Friday's bounce reached $533.34 before fading.

There still isn't enough confirmation to call a bottom.

Here's my updated plan:

527 to 525: Immediate support zone. Buyers need to defend this area and build higher lows. Repeated tests without a sustained bounce keep me cautious.

535 to 538: The first area buyers need to reclaim and HOLD. Former support at 538 now becomes potential resistance. A bounce into this zone that gets sold would keep the setup weak.

550: Upside target if buyers defend support and reclaim 538.

515: Invalidation for my shorter-term bullish trade. Below that, I step aside and reassess.

500: The next major support if the recovery fails.

With $MSFT, $GOOGL, $AMZN earnings and FOMC coming up, there are plenty of catalysts.

Their AI spending outlooks could move the entire semiconductor group.

$SMH remains my proxy for that reaction.

If $SMH holds or reclaims 525 and starts building higher lows, I'm watching Nov 27 550C, targeting 538 first, then 550. Invalidation below 515 on SMH.

If $SMH fails to hold 527, loses 525, and rejects a retest of that zone, Nov 6 500P could work. Watching 515 first, then 500 if selling accelerates. A sustained reclaim of 527 invalidates the breakdown setup.

Those targets and invalidation levels refer to SMH's price.

Options can lose value quickly, especially the shorter-dated puts.

Size for the premium risk and take profits along the way.

My broader scaling plan remains 25% at 535, 25% at 525, and 50% at 500, subject to reassessing the setup.

3 Moving Average Rules for Active Traders

#1) Let the 8 and 21 day moving averages guide your short-term approach.

When the SPX/SPY is above the 8 and 21 day moving averages, I want to stay long with a Portfolio Approach.

Depending on the particular trend, I’ll be long 10-35+ stocks, ETFs, and cryptos that show relative strength.

#2) Don’t fight stocks trending above the 8 & 21 day moving averages. Ride them!

Want to go broke really fast? Bet against a stock trending above the 8 & 21 day moving averages.

#3) When the SPX breaks the 8 & 21 day, Get Tactical. 

That means I start selling longs, starting with names showing relative weakness, and anything I’m not completely bullish on.

posts.name: The Kobeissi Letter
posts.text:
The US junk bond market is under severe pressure:

The effective yield on US CCC-rated and lower-rated high-yield corporate bonds is up to 18.0%, its highest level since the 2020 pandemic.

This figure has surged +500 basis points over the last 6 months, marking its largest 6-month increase since the 2022 bear market.

For perspective, this yield peaked at 45.0% during the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Meanwhile, credit spreads for CCC-rated and lower corporate bonds over Treasuries are up to 13.4%, the widest gap since July 2020.

Over the last 6 months, this gauge has risen +464 basis points, surpassing the 2022 bear market peak of 12.8%.

Cracks are widening beneath the surface of the credit market.

BREAKING: Japanese investors sold -$1.0 billion in foreign long-term bonds in the week ending October 17th, marking their 5th consecutive weekly sale, the longest such streak in 4 years.

Over this period, Japanese investors have sold a cumulative -$22.0 billion in foreign long-term debt securities.

Furthermore, the group sold -$1.0 billion in overseas short-term bonds in the week ending October 17th, marking their 2nd weekly sale over the last 3.

Year-to-date, sales of foreign debt by Japanese investors are up to -$33.0 billion, the largest outflow over the comparable period since 2022.

This also brought 12-month cumulative sales of foreign debt up to -$40.8 billion, the largest such outflow since April 2023.

This trend has been particularly driven by Japanese banks, which are increasing their domestic bond purchases amid historically attractive domestic bond yields.

The global bond market is experiencing a historic shift in investor demand.
